findings.claim: The @AfterEach logout() in the new test class can never do anything: OpenmrsFilter.doFilterInternal ends with finally { Context.clearUserContext(); }, which removes the thread-local UserContext, so Context.logout() returns immediately at its own !isSessionOpen() guard.
findings.evidence: Context.clearUserContext() at api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/Context.java:242-246 calls userContextHolder.remove(); Context.logout() at Context.java:713-716 opens with `if (!isSessionOpen()) return;` and only reaches setUserContext(new UserContext(...)) at line 723 when it actually runs. I ran a probe test (web/src/test/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/ZzProbeTest.java, since deleted) via `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=ZzProbeTest`, which printed: isSessionOpenBeforeFilter=[true], isSessionOpenAfterFilter=[false], isSessionOpenAfterContextLogout=[false]. If the logout had really executed, line 723 would have re-set a UserContext and isSessionOpen() would be true again. So the cleanup is dead code. It is harmless today only because BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.clearSessionAfterEachTest() (api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/test/jupiter/BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java:992-1001) guards its own logout the same way, and @Transactional/@Rollback reverts the data. The concrete trap it leaves: any future test added to this class that calls a Context.* API after doFilterInternal gets APIException("A user context must first be passed to setUserContext()...") from Context.getUserContext() (Context.java:256-266). Either drop the @AfterEach or restore the context after the filter call so the cleanup does what it says.

findings.claim: doFilterInternal_shouldUpdateChangedSessionAttributes seeds the stale locale as Locale.ENGLISH, which counts as 'changed' only because the ambient default locale happens to be en_GB; the test is silently coupled to the default_locale global property.
findings.evidence: The filter compares with Objects.equals(session.getAttribute(name), value) (OpenmrsFilter.java:123) against userContext.getLocale(), which for a freshly created UserContext falls through to LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale() (UserContext.java:349-355). My probe run printed defaultLocale=[en_GB] and equalsLocaleENGLISH=[false], so Locale.ENGLISH ("en") differs and the write happens, giving countWrites(locale)==1. If the test baseline's default_locale GP ever became `en`, the locale half of this test would stop exercising the changed path and fail with `expected: <1> but was: <0>`. Seeding a locale that cannot collide with the default (Locale.JAPANESE), or deriving the stale value from LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale(), removes the coupling. Failure mode is a loud test failure, not silent wrong behavior, hence nit.

what_i_swept:
Confirmed the diff stat first: `git diff eda229b1 d381957e --stat` = 3 files, +279/-12, matching the brief. Read OpenmrsFilter.java in full at d381957 (not just the hunks), plus the full new test class and dataset.

Equivalence proof for the production change: enumerated every reachable combination of (session had a UserContext or not) x (getAuthenticatedUser() null or not) x (getUsername() null / empty / set) and showed the final session state is identical to the base implementation. Two sub-cases needed real verification rather than reasoning. (a) getAuthenticatedUser() is now called on a freshly created UserContext, which the base code never did -- read UserContext.java:211-213 and confirmed it is a plain field getter with no lazy init or DB access, so no new failure or side effect on that path. (b) The null-username case: the base did setAttribute("username", null), which the servlet contract turns into removeAttribute, while the new code may skip the write entirely. Probe run printed oldStyleNullUsernameEndState=[null] and newStyleNullUsernameEndState=[null] -- identical end state, so no regression (note the shipped admin user in core-data carries username="" and logs in by system_id, so empty, not null, is the realistic value, and "" is a normal write either way).

Mutation experiment (the core of 'verified, not eyeballed'): `git show eda229b1:web/.../OpenmrsFilter.java > web/.../OpenmrsFilter.java`, then `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest` -> 3 of 5 fail (shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAnonymous expected 0 was 1, shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAuthenticated expected 0 was 2, shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale expected 1 was 2). Restored with `git checkout --`. This proves the PR's two headline claims -- no writes when unchanged, and no intermediate anonymous write on authenticated requests -- and also proves assertEquals resolved to the primitive (long,long) overload rather than silently boxing Integer vs Long. Baseline at head: 5/5 green.

Outward trace, one level out in every direction I could find:
- Consumers of the two attributes. `git grep '"username"'` across all java/jsp/xml: the only in-repo writer or reader of the session "username" attribute is this filter; the documented consumer is the servlet container's session listing, which reads the value, not the write event. `git grep 'getAttribute("locale")'` finds one hit, InitializationFilterE2ETest:109, which asserts the String "fr" -- tracing that to FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE showed it is the same name "locale", written as a String by InitializationFilter/UpdateFilter and as a Locale by OpenmrsFilter. Checked whether the conditional write breaks that handoff: Objects.equals("fr", Locale) is false across types, so OpenmrsFilter still overwrites. Pre-existing type inconsistency, not touched by this PR.
- Attribute listeners. Dropping the per-request write removes attributeReplaced callbacks, so I checked for listeners that depend on them. `git grep HttpSessionAttributeListener` = 0 hits repo-wide; positive control on the same pipeline, `git grep -c HttpSessionListener` = 14 hits in web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/Listener.java, so the zero is a real absence and not a broken search. Listener.java only dispatches to HttpSessionListener beans. Also confirmed UserContext implements Serializable only (UserContext.java:49), not HttpSessionBindingListener, so no bound/unbound side effects.
- Lifecycle. Traced Context.setUserContext/clearUserContext (Context.java:232-246) and found the holder is a plain ThreadLocal<Object[]> with set/remove, not a stack -- that is what produced finding correctness-1.
- The state transitions the tests do NOT cover, which are the ones that would actually hurt if the conditional write were wrong. Ran a second probe (ZzProbe2Test, since deleted) driving one session and one UserContext through anonymous -> authenticate -> logout with the filter run between each: afterFirstAnonymous=[-anonymous user-], afterLogin=[test_user], afterLogout=[-anonymous user-], usernameAttributeStillPresent=[true]. So a logged-out session does not retain the previous user's name, which was the one outcome that would have been a blocking defect.
- Test fixture. Verified web/src/test/resources/OpenmrsFilterTest-initial.xml is a verbatim copy of the established row in AdministrationServiceTest-globalproperties.xml and EncounterServiceTest-initialData.xml, that person_id=501 exists and is not voided in standardTestDataset.xml:251, and that no other fixture claims user_id 5506 with a conflicting username. Rollback hygiene is proven by the fact that two tests in the class execute that dataset in the same JVM run without a PK collision.
- Concurrency. Walked the check-then-act in setSessionAttributeIfChanged for two parallel requests on one session: both requests read the same shared UserContext and compute the same value, so the worst case is a duplicate write of an identical value, never a lost update. The username attribute has always lagged authentication by one request, in the base code too, so that is not a regression.

Three passes. Pass 1 (equivalence + mutation) surfaced nothing in production code; pass 2 (lifecycle + outward trace) surfaced correctness-1 and correctness-2; pass 3 (concurrency, fixture, attribute listeners, login/logout transitions, assertEquals overload) surfaced nothing substantive, so convergence is satisfied.

This matters because the UserContext stored under __openmrs_user_context is mutated in place (authenticate, logout, setLocale, setUserLocation) and is never re-setAttribute'd, so under such a manager the old unconditional username/locale writes would have piggy-backed those mutations into the replicated copy. I have no clustered container here to test it. I did not raise it as a finding because the reasoning cuts against it: the standard attribute-delta managers (Tomcat DeltaManager, Spring Session) replicate only the attribute that was written, so they would not have carried the in-place UserContext mutation before this change either; the user-visible locale change does get written on the following request because the filter compares against userContext.getLocale(); and the ticket explicitly asks for the redundant write to be dropped.
